comment: ACTION-EXECUTOR-16 and -23: the reserved snapshot sealing key names and the custody refusal, mirrored by the CLI bundle check. The API side (packages/curie-internal/src/curie_internal/sealing_key.py, apps/api/src/curie_api/bundles.py::sealing_key_custody_issues) and the CLI side (cli/src/sealing_key.rs) cannot share code across Python and Rust, so both read this file. `reason` is the refusal with `{name}` substituted; `reasons` is it formatted for each name. `references` are texts the MCP client expands from the sandbox environment and the reserved names each references, in sorted order. Each `bundles` case is a bundle whose `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` declares `plugin_secrets` (when present) and whose `connectors.yaml` is `connectors_yaml` (when present); `refused` is every refusal in order, each naming the reserved name (the message is `reasons[name]`) and the location. An empty `refused` is an accepted bundle. Placeholder values only.
reason: {name} is a reserved snapshot sealing key: it must reach only the hosted connector, so it may be declared only as a SecretRef (`- name: {name}` with `from_secret:`) on that connector

reasons.SNAPSHOT_SEALING_KEY: SNAPSHOT_SEALING_KEY is a reserved snapshot sealing key: it must reach only the hosted connector, so it may be declared only as a SecretRef (`- name: SNAPSHOT_SEALING_KEY` with `from_secret:`) on that connector
reasons.SNAPSHOT_SEALING_KEYS_RETAINED: SNAPSHOT_SEALING_KEYS_RETAINED is a reserved snapshot sealing key: it must reach only the hosted connector, so it may be declared only as a SecretRef (`- name: SNAPSHOT_SEALING_KEYS_RETAINED` with `from_secret:`) on that connector
